name: Gametape Licks
tagline: A guitarist's study of the details behind great playing.
description: Guitar lessons that teach the why behind the notes and the pattern recognition to adapt to the band, the pace and the moment.

home.kicker: Guitar lessons for players who listen
home.title: Play what the music is asking for.
home.lede: Each lesson takes one idea apart. You learn why it works, where it shows up again and how to hear it coming, so you can use it in any key, at any tempo, with any band.
home.seoTitle: Gametape Licks | Guitar Lessons That Teach the Why Behind the Notes

method.title: Built for the moment you cannot plan for
method.body: A pattern works in every song that shares it. These lessons train you to spot the pattern while the band is playing, so you can follow along when the tempo shifts or the chords change on you.

steps.title: See it
steps.body: Fretboards you can change. Type in a chord progression and every diagram redraws for your chords.

steps.title: Know why
steps.body: Short explanations of what each note does against the chord, in plain words.

steps.title: Recognize it
steps.body: Rules that repeat across keys and progressions, so a new tune looks familiar by the second bar.

steps.title: Use it live
steps.body: Drills inspired by players you love, like Trey Anastasio, built to run at tempo with a backing track.

library.title: One idea at a time, in any key.
library.lede: Start at Lesson 1 and work forward, or pick a topic. Every lesson has a printable PDF you can bring to rehearsal.

about.title: About Gametape Licks
paragraphs: Gametape Licks is a place to study guitar the way a team studies game film. Pick one idea, slow it down and look at exactly what is happening.
Each lesson shows why the idea works, where it shows up again and how to hear it coming. The goal is to know where to go when the band does something you did not plan for.
The lessons are free to read and print. They describe approaches heard in the playing of musicians we admire. None of them are note-for-note transcriptions.

topics.name: Chord tones
topics.blurb: Aim at the notes that define each chord, the 3rds above all, and your solos start to follow the changes.

topics.name: Phrasing
topics.blurb: How a line breathes, where it starts and where it lands. Guitar phrasing lessons for players who want their solos to sound like sentences.

topics.name: Ear training
topics.blurb: Hear the chord change before it arrives. Ear training for guitarists who want to adapt to the band in the moment.

topics.name: Rhythm
topics.blurb: Time, feel and placement for guitarists. Rhythm lessons that lock your lines to the band.

author.name: Mike Caprio
bio: Mike Caprio is an NYC-based advertising and media executive with more than 25 years of experience building and scaling global advertising, data and video technology businesses. He is known for first-principles thinking and decisive execution, and he brings the same habits to guitar.

He plays blues and jam-band guitar, and he is the guitarist in The Band Project. He writes these lessons to share what he learns from studying the players he admires: the chord tone, the reason it works and the pattern to listen for next time.
